name: iam-policy-check
title: IAM Policy Check
description: Reads each IAM or S3 bucket policy statement back in plain words (who, what, on what, under which condition) and flags admin and service:* wildcards, Resource "*", Principal "*" that S3 would call public, NotAction/NotPrincipal traps and wide iam:PassRole, with scoped fixes.

meta.stops: Helps catch an S3 bucket made public by a policy
meta.summary: Reads an AWS IAM or S3 bucket policy back in plain words and flags grants far wider than intended, such as a bucket made public.
meta.server: Validate policies with IAM Access Analyzer in CI and keep S3 Block Public Access on at the account level.
catches: Full-admin and service:* action wildcards, and Resource "*"
Principal "*" that S3 Block Public Access treats as public, including conditions that don't narrow it
Public reads and writes on a bucket
Allow with NotAction, and NotPrincipal traps
iam:PassRole on every role, with an iam:PassedToService fix
limits: Static review of one policy; it can't see SCPs, permission boundaries, session policies or resource policies elsewhere
Doesn't evaluate a request the way the IAM engine does; use IAM Access Analyzer or the policy simulator to confirm
Suggested fixes (your account, used actions) depend on the inputs you pass
a11y: Text area has a label, aria-invalid when errors exist, and is described by the status
Status uses role=status; icons are aria-hidden
Each issue has a labelled button that selects its line; focus returns to a nearby control after a fix

sources.label: AWS: Blocking public access to your Amazon S3 storage (The meaning of "public")

rules.note: Informational; check the official source. Confirmed that non-public requires fixed values for principals or aws:SourceIp CIDR sets. The exact CIDR width AWS counts as public and the IAM element reference were not re-checked this round.
